subject: Lumenary load test: k6/Locust handoff + streaming SLO recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@lumenary.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@lumenary.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Lumenary load test: k6/Locust handoff + streaming SLO recap

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick written recap and clear next steps so we can get the customer-driven run moving. Please reply with any corrections.

Recap (what we agreed)
- Test model: lumenary-gen-2 (open-variant) on Redwood Dedicated pool.
- Primary objectives: validate streaming concurrency and tail latency under customer workload; verify graceful fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.
- Key SLO targets (customer-side): p95 inference latency < 250ms for short responses (<=128 tokens), p99 < 600ms; streaming concurrency target = 400 concurrent sessions; sustained throughput target = ~1,800 requests/min (30 RPS) for non-streaming baseline.
- Test phases: Phase A (ramp + warmup): 30 min ramp to target concurrency; Phase B (soak): 120 min at target with 2x short-burst spikes (5 min each) to validate autoscale/fallback.
- Metrics of interest: client-observed p50/p95/p99, server-side tail latency, cold-cache vs warm-cache runs, KV cache hit-rate, error rate, token/sec and partial-response metrics for streaming.

Customer responsibilities (Lumenary)
- Provide IP allowlist for your load generators and confirm test window.
- We'll accept either k6 or Locust scripts. You indicated preference to run Locust first to exercise streaming and then k6 for repeatability. Attachments: I attached our recommended k6 profile (lumenary_k6_profile_v1.js) plus a Locust streaming harness (locustfile_streaming.py) for reference.
- Create a test account or provide us the test API key: scope limited to /inference, rate-limited, 30-day TTL.

Redwood responsibilities
- Provide an instrumented probe endpoint and a short-lived test API key for your scripts (we'll create the key after you confirm allowlist and time window).
- Preflight run 24 hours before the window with a small synthetic load to validate IP routing and credentials.
- Engineering on-call during the window; we'll capture server-side traces and share a post-test report within 48 hours.

Proposed test window (please confirm in your TZ)
- Aug 7, 2028 16:00–20:00 PDT (convertible if this conflicts — we can shift ±1 day or swap to 09:00–13:00 PDT).

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Do you want us to seed a warm KV cache before the soak? (recommended: yes — we can run a 20-min warmup script).
2) Will the streaming sessions originate from three IP blocks or a corporate pool? Please share exact CIDR ranges for allowlisting.
3) Do you need us to run the cold-cache pass (server restarted) as a separate short test?

Next steps
- Alex / Sasha: confirm window and send IP ranges + preferred script order.
- Redwood (Vivek): provision test API key and probe endpoint once allowlist confirmed.
- Mutual action plan: I attached a short MAP PDF (mutual-action-plan-LUM-49.pdf) — please review and comment.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the preflight 24 hours prior once we have the allowlist.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: lumenary_k6_profile_v1.js (k6 script), locustfile_streaming.py (Locust script), mutual-action-plan-LUM-49.pdf

From: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@lumenary.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@lumenary.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumenary load test: k6/Locust handoff + streaming SLO recap

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We want both cold-cache and warm-cache passes. Cold-cache first early in the window (10 min) then warm-seed and run the ramp/soak. The cold pass is important for our client-side tail behavior.
- We will originate traffic from three AWS regions: us-west-2 (54.240.0.0/12), us-east-1 (52.0.0.0/11), eu-west-1 (18.0.0.0/12) — these are our egress pools; let us know if you need more specific EC2 ENI IPs.
- Regarding scripts: we'll run Locust streaming harness to emulate long-lived SSE/WebSocket-style sessions and then run the k6 profile for a controlled soak. We'll attach our Locust scenario tomorrow.

One operational note: when you say p95 < 250ms, is that measured observer-side (client) or server-side? For our internal SLAs we look at client-observed times (including transport). If Redwood will provide both, that's perfect — we can reconcile differences after the test.

Confirming tentative window Aug 7 16:00–20:00 PDT. We'll send the full Locust file and expected user behavior by EOD tomorrow.

—Alex
Alex Reyes
Head of SRE Engineering, Lumenary Systems
ops+loadtests@lumenary.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@lumenary.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@lumenary.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 18:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumenary load test: k6/Locust handoff + streaming SLO recap

Alex — thanks, perfect. Answers inline below and a few updates: 

> One operational note: when you say p95 < 250ms, is that measured observer-side (client) or server-side?
We will capture both. In the MAP/acceptance criteria we’ll present: (A) client-observed p95 (what your users see) and (B) server-side application p95 (Redwood instrumentation). For the official pass we will use client-observed p95 as the authoritative metric, but we’ll correlate with server traces to debug.

IP allowlist — confirm we should accept the CIDRs you listed. For the preflight we’ll open temporary access for the three blocks you provided. If you can give the exact ENI IPs the day before that’s ideal but the CIDR blocks are fine for now.

Test accounts / credentials
- We'll provision a short-lived test API key once you confirm CIDRs and the final window. Key will be scoped to: inference:read, inference:stream. TTL 48 hours.

Attached I’m including the k6 and Locust reference scripts. A few notes on the scripts:
- k6 profile includes a prefix-warmup option to seed the KV cache (set KV_WARMUP=true to enable).
- Locust file creates long-lived HTTP streaming sessions (via SSE) with keepalive heartbeats every 25s.

Operational contacts during window
- Redwood on-call (Vivek Kulkarni) — +1 (650) 555-0199 (primary)
- Escalation: Ben Carter — ben_carter@redwood.ai

I'll provision the probe endpoint and test key after you confirm the CIDRs. We'll also open a dedicated Slack channel for the weekend (or the day-of) coordination and drop the preflight logs there.

—
Marissa

- Ask infra to bump streaming buffer defaults for the duration of the test window so we don't prematurely drop connections (we'll roll this back after the test).
- We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and p99.9 (tail) from the server and provide live dashboards in the Slack channel.

Ben: please standby to escalate if we observe cascading failures during the soak.

—Vivek

Thanks — confirmed. We will: 
- Send the final Locust file and an optional small synthetic k6 snippet by tonight (EOD PST).
- Confirm exact ENI IPs the day before; CIDRs work for now.
- Run the cold-cache pass first (10 minutes), then the warmup + ramp + soak as specified.

One last question: for our internal reporting we tag passes by client-observed p95. Could Redwood include the client-observed p95 times in the post-test artifact (CSV + Grafana snapshots) so we can ingest directly into our QA dashboard? Also, do you have a preferred format for the test run metadata (start/stop timestamps, seed config)?

If you can attach a small JSON schema or example for the metadata we’ll align our ingestion. Happy to jump on a 15-minute sync if needed tomorrow.

—Alex
